title: Melvins & Napalm Death — Savage Imperial Death March
author: Roger Batty
excerpt: When I first heard about this collaboration between The Melvins and Napalm Death, I thought I had a good idea how this was going to sound — but aside from a few tracks, this album sounds nothing like I was expecting. And I think it's fair to say that for the most part, Savage Imperial Death March is very much a dive into the odd, off-kilter, and downright weird. To say Savage Imperial Death March was very much of a weird and wonderful surprise is an understatement. Apparently, the album was a fifty/ fifty collab, and together they conjured up such an unpredictable and keenly experimental yet entertaining record, which really is unlike anything else.
label: Ipecac Recordings

title: Sunn O)))))) — Sunn O))))))
author: Roger Batty
excerpt: After spending the last decade and a half or so trying to expand upon, cross-genre pollinate, and generally do something different with their monolithic sound, this tenth studio album from prime doom droners Sunn O)))))) finds them very much returning to their roots, but with way more layers of guitars and pure crushing weightiness about it. When I first got this album, it barely left my stereo, and at points I had to literally forcefully remove it to play other stuff. Not only is self-titled a true & proper return to form from Sunn O)))))), but it's one of 2026's highlights.
label: Sub Pop

title: Pig Peasant — Ossabaw Island Hog
author: Roger Batty
excerpt: Ossabaw Island Hog is a twenty-minute slice of choppy and bass-pummelling walling from this Old Town, Maine-based project. Throughout the track has an oddly soothing quality about it, and I could have easily played this for another twenty, thirty, or even forty minutes. Built around a chugging 'n' blunt low end, surrounded by choppy, slightly hiss-bound Mids. The whole 'wall' has a decidedly muddy/woozy feel about it, and really, this pulls you deeper into the 'wall' — to fully enjoy the textural patterns on offer here.
label: Dying Monolith HNW

title: Raté — Bruit De Fond
author: Roger Batty
excerpt: Bruit De Fond is an example of churning walled noise nihilism from Bordeaux's Raté. It's a single thirty-four-minute track, which remains terminal hope-battering & unbreakable over its full length. The track is built around a thick, full and rapid blend of constantly rolling bass churn, choppy mids, and cluttering hiss-bound subtones. It makes for a very clamouring and airless 'wall' — which brought to mind having a panic attack in rush hour city traffic.
label: Self Release

title: Necrotik Fissure — Was
author: Roger Batty
excerpt: Here's seventy-eight minutes' worth of barrenly searing 'n' crudely whizzing HNW from this Hungarian project. Necrotik Fissure has been active since the early 2010's, been both prolific and unflinchingly extreme in its releasing of the walled noise form. The single track is a rapid and totally engulfing affair — thick weave bringing together a constantly rolling 'n' rearing bass tone, a whizzing grind, with a few cluttering/baying subtones. Was is another longform, searing, and totally unforgiving example of the wall noise form.
label: Self Release
